items.title: Michael Weiss interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 22, 2021
items.q: There’s a great interview with Pat Metheny I saw recently

ctx.x: It was used as sort of a button, the end, they lived happily ever after, on to the next. Yeah. It’s a little marker. A melodic marker. Yeah. Using and re-using your material, repetition or sequencing is the hallmark of a good song. And it can be referred to as a hook, but any — I talk about this, I recently did an online composition and arranging master class called “Getting More Out of Your Tunes” where almost any good song has some repetition in it, has some sequencing. You can’t just have a continuous run-on…

Yeah, that’s a good observation. Well this has really been a fascinating conversation and I congratulate you on your career so far. And I hope that you will be thought of as one of those people like when you apprenticed with Johnny Griffin that people will be doing that with you.
